principle: Each project belongs to one system family, has one primary role, and carries orthogonal traits. Scores are comparable only inside the same score profile.

system_families.name: Memory systems
system_families.definition: Systems whose primary value is capturing, organizing, preserving, retrieving, or reasoning over durable knowledge.

system_families.name: Agent systems
system_families.definition: Systems whose primary value is planning and taking actions through tools on a person's behalf.

primary_roles.name: Human-first PKM / workspace
primary_roles.definition: A user-facing system whose canonical workflow is human writing, organizing, linking, and revisiting knowledge.

primary_roles.name: AI knowledge app / RAG brain
primary_roles.definition: A user-facing assistant that ingests documents or connected sources and answers, searches, summarizes, or automates over them.

primary_roles.name: External agent-memory service
primary_roles.definition: A replaceable library or service that extracts, stores, retrieves, and manages durable memories through an SDK, API, or tool protocol.

primary_roles.name: Temporal context / knowledge-graph engine
primary_roles.definition: Infrastructure that represents entities, relationships, provenance, and changing truth over time.

primary_roles.name: Human–agent memory bridge
primary_roles.definition: A compatibility layer that exposes human-owned files or workspaces to multiple agents.

primary_roles.name: Ambient capture / lifelogging
primary_roles.definition: A passive collector that records digital activity without requiring deliberate note creation.

primary_roles.name: Retrieval / storage infrastructure
primary_roles.definition: A low-level vector, graph, lexical, or multimodal store used to build memory systems.

primary_roles.name: Research / benchmark / reference
primary_roles.definition: A survey, benchmark, course, template, or catalog that informs memory implementation.

primary_roles.name: Coding agent
primary_roles.definition: An interactive agent that reads, edits, runs, and reasons about software projects.

primary_roles.name: Research agent
primary_roles.definition: An agent that plans multi-step information gathering and synthesizes cited findings.

primary_roles.name: Browser / computer-use agent
primary_roles.definition: An agent specialized in operating browsers, desktops, or other graphical interfaces.

primary_roles.name: Stateful agent runtime / harness
primary_roles.definition: A persistent agent runtime that owns identity, durable state, skills, schedules, and memory lifecycle.

primary_roles.name: Coding-agent workflow / skill stack
primary_roles.definition: Prompts, roles, tools, and process that turn coding agents into a repeatable software-delivery system.

primary_roles.name: Multi-agent orchestrator
primary_roles.definition: A system for coordinating specialized agents, handoffs, workflows, and shared execution.

primary_roles.name: Agent framework / SDK
primary_roles.definition: A developer framework for building tool-using, controllable, observable agent applications.

architectures.name: Vector / embedding index
architectures.note: An architecture trait, not a product category.

license_scopes.name: Open-source core plus restricted enterprise code

dimensions.definition: Direct usefulness as a personal or agentic second brain.
Local-first behavior, exportability, privacy, and user control.
Open formats, APIs, adapters, and model/provider portability.
Retrieval, temporal handling, provenance, consolidation, and contradiction management.
Setup and maintenance burden for a technically capable individual.
Adoption, maintenance, documentation, and production readiness.
Consistency and correctness on the tasks the system claims to handle.
Breadth, quality, and composability of tool invocation.
Ability to plan and complete meaningful multi-step work.
Approvals, steering, boundaries, inspectability, and safe interruption.
Tracing, checkpoints, error visibility, replay, and recovery.
Local execution, privacy, exportability, and operator control.
Provider, tool, protocol, and deployment portability.
Adoption, maintenance, documentation, and production readiness.
